clue.text: Stalks latecomer regularly, often smoking weed?

definitions.note: lemongrass is sold and cooked as stalks, so the plural noun stands for the plant

indicators.note: 'regularly' asks for letters at a fixed interval, here every third one

parts.note: every third letter of LatEcoMer: L, E, M
someone habitually smoking weed is 'on grass' (grass = cannabis)

explanation.surface: Someone who turns up late is always seen puffing on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalks' looks like a verb about following someone, but it is the plural noun. The regular letters are every third one, not the usual alternate ones; 'on grass' is slang for being a regular cannabis user.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by the part used: the plant reaches the kitchen as woody stalks.

clue.text: Spandex: extremely crass clothing

indicators.note: read as a verb, 'clothing' means dressing or wrapping round, so the two words wrap the answer

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict: skin-tight stretch fabric is the height of bad taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' reads as the garments made of Spandex, but it is a verb: the words clothe, or wrap around, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional equivalence: the British trade name for the stretch fibre that Americans call by the other name.

clue.text: Is musing cryptically around noon an indication of negativity?

indicators.note: 'around' puts the scrambled letters on either side of the next piece
'cryptically' says the words are to be read in a coded, scrambled form

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Is brooding over something at midday a sign of a pessimistic mood?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'negativity' is about mood; the definition means it in the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: the dash in front of a number shows it is below zero.

clue.text: Local communities bug heroin suspect with violent criminals

indicators.note: as an adjective 'suspect' means dubious, so the letters before it are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Residents wiretap a gang they think is dealing heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' and 'suspect' both look like police verbs, but 'bug' is just letters and 'suspect' is an adjective saying those letters are out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: districts of a town together with the people who live there.

clue.text: One who regrets quietly quitting is to compete again

indicators.note: the letter for 'quietly' is 'quitting', leaving the word it sat in

parts.note: p = piano, quietly in music; this letter goes

explanation.surface: A remorseful player who walked away wants to come back into the contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quietly quitting' passes for the office buzzword for doing the bare minimum, but it is P leaving the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: signing up for a race or contest a second time.

clue.text: Guy's lump occasionally doesn't settle in the evening

parts.note: a guy is a stay, a rope bracing a tent or mast; the 's is kept

indicators.note: 'occasionally' means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A man with a lump on him cannot get comfortable at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is not a man here but a guy rope, which is also called a stay.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: not going to bed at night is the opposite of settling down for it.

clue.text: Old-fashioned haircut for a male

parts.note: per = for a, as in 'per day'
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A dated hairstyle suited to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a' looks like filler connecting haircut to male, but it supplies PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: chemically set curls, a style associated with the 1980s.

clue.text: Provide online joke?

parts.note: e- = electronic, online, as in email
a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Posting gags on the internet as a service to others.
explanation.walkthrough: The e- prefix of email and e-commerce gives 'online' as the single letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to supply someone with what they need.

clue.text: Shabby way of working by playhouse; November run cancelled

indicators.note: 'by' means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: MO = modus operandi, a way of working
R = run in cricket scoring; this letter goes
November is N in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A tatty production at the theatre has its November run called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties 'November run cancelled' together as a theatre booking; in fact N is added and only the R goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: cloth chewed full of holes by moths, hence worn out and tatty.

clue.text: Penny longed to meet British ex-Prime Minister, almost succeeded, which resulted in disturbances

indicators.note: 'almost' means not quite all, so the name loses its last letter
one piece meets the next, so they are joined end to end

parts.note: Clement ATTLEE, Labour Prime Minister 1945-51, without his last letter

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny's longing to meet a former British premier ended in riots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' reads as a woman's name, but it is the coin abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: set-piece violent clashes are an extreme kind of public disorder.

clue.text: Brief caught working with Russia and its allies before start of election

indicators.note: 'with' simply adds one piece to the next

parts.note: on = working, as a machine is on
the Commonwealth of Independent States, the post-Soviet bloc

indicators.note: 'start of' takes just the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A lawyer's brief is exposed as having worked for Moscow just before polling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like a lawyer or a set of instructions; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: short and to the point.

clue.text: Sample of "Float like a butterfly, sting like a be"?

indicators.note: 'be' is BEE printed without its last letter, showing that the quotation is cut short the same way

parts.note: Muhammad Ali's own boast about his boxing
the whole line is a famous quotation

explanation.surface: An excerpt from Muhammad Ali's most famous line about his boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: The typo is the instruction: 'be' is BEE without its last letter, so the Ali quote loses its last letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical synonym: a chemist's measured portion taken from a larger quantity for testing.

clue.text: Seethes at debauched lovers of Grace?

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted, led astray, so the letters are knocked out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone is fuming at the dissolute admirers of a woman called Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital G makes Grace look like a woman's name; it is grace in the sense of beauty and elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: people devoted to beauty and refinement love elegance.

clue.text: Manage to capture Serbian leader in thicket

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside
a leader goes first, so only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A fugitive Serbian leader is caught hiding in dense undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' reads as a head of state, but it only means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a small wood of close-growing trees and bushes.

clue.text: Character eating into company's capital

indicators.note: something eating into a word ends up inside it

parts.note: an air is a manner or character, an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Someone is eating into a firm's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is set up as a firm's money, but it is a capital city; 's is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the seat of government of Egypt.

clue.text: Reduction of the reaction times of a city lass in transit

indicators.note: letters in transit are on the move, so they will not arrive in the order they set out

explanation.surface: A girl from town on the move reacts more quickly than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In transit' reads as a girl travelling, but it says the letters are moving about.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by effect: a catalyst speeds a chemical change, so the time it takes shrinks.

clue.text: Play the part of salesman with grudge

indicators.note: 'with' simply adds the second piece to the first

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: An actor takes the role of a travelling salesman who bears a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grudge' looks like a noun the salesman carries; it has to be read as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical sense: to portray a character on stage or in art.

clue.text: Obtained sacred text, rewritten to remove sacrilegious introduction

indicators.note: text that is rewritten comes out in a new arrangement
'to remove' takes that letter out of the fodder
an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of Sacrilegious, the letter taken away

explanation.surface: A holy scripture is revised to cut out an irreverent opening.
explanation.walkthrough: With the S of 'sacred' gone, the nine remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: drawn out or got hold of, as information or a tooth.

clue.text: Reflect on 'agitato' being instruction for a musician

indicators.note: agitato is Italian for agitated, and agitated letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A player ponders the marking 'agitato' on the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitato' is a real score marking, so it hides well as an instruction to stir the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the sign at the start of a stave tells a cellist or trombonist which pitch each line stands for.

clue.text: Film serial killer next to new desk

indicators.note: 'next to' puts the second piece right beside the first

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter of The Silence of the Lambs

explanation.surface: A movie murderer is placed beside a brand-new desk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'new desk' a phrase; 'new' belongs to the wordplay and 'desk' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific kind: a sloping reading stand used by a speaker or in church.

clue.text: Card play is excellent, supported by system's odds

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is supported sits on top, so the second piece goes underneath
'odds' means the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A card player's strategy is sound, backed by a betting system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' suggests betting but means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge term: an attempt to win a trick with a lower card while a higher one is still out.

clue.text: Don't declare staff

definitions.note: the verb phrase is read run together as one word
definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side that declares ends its innings early; one that doesn't carries on at the crease
a staff here is a short stick, as carried by a conductor or relay runner

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket side that doesn't declare will BAT ON; run together that is the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: continuing to bat instead of closing the innings, and a short stick or rod of office.

clue.text: Perhaps arm officers, to begin with, in prison

parts.note: an arm is one example of a limb

indicators.note: 'to begin with' takes only the opening letter

explanation.surface: A suggestion that prison officers could be issued weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like a verb, give weapons to, but it is a noun: an arm, perhaps, is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An old slang sense: a place of confinement, a jail.

clue.text: Pile of rector's neck hair covering opening in sink

definitions.note: a pile is a large house, so 'pile of rector's' is the rector's house

indicators.note: hair covering something lies around it, so the letters wrap the next piece

parts.note: the long hair on a horse's or lion's neck

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman's clump of neck hair is clogging the plughole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' looks like a heap of hair, but it is a grand house. The answer is strictly a minister's home, stretched here to a rector.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the house a church provides for its clergyman.

clue.text: Force prisoners to study

parts.note: to train is to study for a skill, as to train as a nurse

explanation.surface: Making inmates attend classes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction; 'to' only sits between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a verb: to compel or oblige.

clue.text: Asian river, with rising level of nitrogen, is focus of infection

indicators.note: N is nitrogen's symbol, and in a down entry it rises one level, swapping places with the I above it

explanation.surface: Rising nitrogen levels in an Asian river make it the source of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'rising level' sounds like pollution data; the letters of the river do the moving instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term: the spot where bacteria settle and multiply, the seat of a disease.

clue.text: Function to end with no date for a restart

definitions.text: with no date for a restart

parts.note: die = end, come to an end

explanation.surface: A computer function set to stop with no date given for rebooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party or a software routine, but it is the trigonometric one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase, 'without a day': a meeting adjourned this way has no fixed date to resume.

clue.text: Acknowledged to be unhappy without musical instrument

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense means outside, so the first word goes around the second

explanation.surface: A musician admits to being miserable without their instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, which is the trap; the old meaning, outside, is the one at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: greeted or recognised with a gesture.

clue.text: Disheartened, cries about issue

indicators.note: a word's heart is its middle letter, so disheartened loses it
'about' turns the word round

parts.note: WEEPS with its middle letter, its heart, removed

explanation.surface: Someone downcast weeps over a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a problem to cry about, but it is a verb, to pour out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a verb: to pour out or gush forth.

clue.text: Nudes ride in a cavalier fashion across Sweden, revealing bottoms

indicators.note: the scrambled letters stretch across the next piece, enclosing it
done cavalierly means carelessly, so the letters land any old way

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Naked riders gallop carelessly through Sweden, showing their backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' puns on horsemen, fitting 'ride', while telling you to jumble the letters; 'bottoms' in the surface is a joke about bare bums.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the lower surfaces of things.
